name: Chavacano (Caviteño / Chabacano de Cavite)

ancestors.notes: Spanish is the lexifier; written with the Spanish alphabet.
Tagalog substrate (Manila Bay area): phonology and grammar.

notes: Caviteño Chabacano (Chabacano de Cavite), a Manila-Bay Spanish-lexifier creole of Cavite City, Luzon, Philippines — moribund, distinct from Zamboangueño (cbk-zam). STUB WITH NO GRAPHEME TABLE: this spec maps nothing and transcribes every input to the empty string. `parent` records genealogy only and never carries data, so nothing is inherited from cbk-zam, and no `graphemes_base` edge is declared because Zamboangueño's table would be wrong here. Sippola's APiCS description of Cavite Chabacano lists /v/, /ʃ/ and /d͡ʒ/ as phonemes, together with /ʔ/ and /ŋ/ from the Tagalog substrate; the Zamboangueño map has no reading for any of them and reads ⟨v⟩ as [b] (Lipski 1987). The written variety is also unsettled — APiCS describes the documented lect as almost entirely written Cavite Chabacano produced by language activists — so a grapheme map has to be derived from a Manila-Bay description rather than borrowed. Documented differences from Zamboangueño (TMA particles ta/ya/di, Tagalog rather than Visayan substrate) are likewise unencoded.
